**[SECTION 1: DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following capitalized terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Section 1 shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Agreement.

**1.1 \"Affiliates\"** means, with respect to a party, any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such party. For purposes of this definition, \"control\" means the direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or equivalent ownership interest of an entity, or the power to direct the management or policies of an entity by contract or otherwise.

**1.2 \"Aggregated De-Identified Data\"** means data derived from Customer Data that has been aggregated and de-identified such that it does not identify Customer or any individual.

**1.3 \"Authorized Users\"** means the individual employees, contractors, and agents of Customer who are authorized by Customer to access and use the Platform under this Agreement, not to exceed the number of named users specified in the applicable Order Form.

**1.4 \"Business Associate Agreement\" or \"BAA\"** means an agreement as described in Section 7.5 of this Agreement, addressing the parties\' respective obligations with respect to Protected Health Information under HIPAA.

**1.5 \"Confidential Information\"** means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other party (the \"**Receiving Party**\"), whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, that is designated as confidential at the time of disclosure or that, given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure, would reasonably be understood to be confidential. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, business plans, financial information, technical data, product roadmaps, pricing, customer lists, and the terms and conditions of this Agreement. Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or action by the Receiving Party; (b) was rightfully in the Receiving Party\'s possession prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, without restriction on disclosure; (c) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information; or (d) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality.

**1.6 \"Customer Data\"** means all data, information, content, and materials submitted, uploaded, transmitted, or otherwise made available by or on behalf of Customer or its Authorized Users to, through, or in connection with the Platform, including but not limited to patient records, clinical data, operational data, and Protected Health Information (as defined in 45 CFR § 160.103).

**1.7 \"Documentation\"** means Vaultline\'s standard user guides, technical manuals, specifications, API documentation, and online help materials for the Platform, as updated by Vaultline from time to time and made generally available to its customers.

**1.8 \"Effective Date\"** means November 1, 2024.

**1.9 \"Fees\"** means the fees payable by Customer to Vaultline under this Agreement, as set forth in the Order Form attached hereto as Exhibit A, and as may be adjusted from time to time in accordance with Section 3.3.

**1.10 \"Implementation Services\"** means the setup, configuration, data migration, integration, and training services to be performed by Vaultline as described in Section 4 and the Order Form.

**1.11 \"Initial Term\"** means the period commencing on the Effective Date and expiring on October 31, 2027, unless earlier terminated in accordance with Section 11.

**1.12 \"Order Form\"** means the order form attached hereto as Exhibit A, which sets forth the specific Platform modules, number of Authorized Users, authorized locations, Fees, and other commercial terms applicable to Customer\'s subscription.

**1.13 \"Platform\"** means Vaultline Prism, Vaultline\'s proprietary cloud-based clinical analytics platform, together with all updates, upgrades, patches, enhancements, modifications, and new releases thereof that Vaultline may provide to Customer during the Term as part of the subscription.

**1.14 \"Professional Services\"** means any consulting, training, advisory, customization, or other professional services provided by Vaultline to Customer outside the scope of the Implementation Services and standard support obligations set forth in Section 5, as may be set forth in a separately executed statement of work or change order.

**1.15 \"Renewal Term\"** means each successive one (1)-year renewal period following the Initial Term, as described in Section 11.2.

**1.16 \"Security Incident\"** means any unauthorized access to, acquisition of, use of, or disclosure of Customer Data, whether by Vaultline personnel, Subprocessors, or any third party.

**1.17 \"Service Level Agreement\" or \"SLA\"** means the service level commitments, uptime guarantees, and related remedies set forth in Exhibit B attached hereto.

**1.18 \"Subprocessor\"** means any third party engaged by Vaultline to process Customer Data on Vaultline\'s behalf in connection with the provision of the Platform or related services, including hosting providers and infrastructure service providers. The parties acknowledge that the Platform is hosted on Amazon Web Services (\"**AWS**\") infrastructure located in the us-east-1 (Northern Virginia) and us-west-2 (Oregon) regions of the United States, and that AWS is a Subprocessor under this Agreement.

**1.19 \"Term\"** means, collectively, the Initial Term and any Renewal Terms.

**1.20 \"Third-Party Components\"** means any software, code, libraries, or tools owned by third parties that are incorporated into or distributed with the Platform.

**1.21 \"Virus\"** means any software code or program designed to disrupt, disable, harm, or otherwise impede the normal operation of a computer system, including without limitation computer viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, spyware, adware, or other malicious code.

**[SECTION 2: GRANT OF RIGHTS; ACCESS TO PLATFORM]{.underline}**

**2.1 License Grant.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and Customer\'s payment of all applicable Fees, Vaultline hereby grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable right to access and use the Platform during the Term, solely for Customer\'s internal business purposes and in accordance with the Documentation. The foregoing right includes the right for up to four hundred (400) named Authorized Users to access the Platform, as specified in the Order Form (Exhibit A). Access to the Platform is permitted across Customer\'s fourteen (14) authorized clinic locations as identified in the Order Form. Each Authorized User shall be assigned a unique login credential, and login credentials may not be shared among multiple individuals. Customer may reassign a named user license from one individual to another on a permanent basis, provided that the total number of active Authorized Users does not exceed four hundred (400) at any time during the Term.

**2.2 Restrictions.** Customer shall not, and shall not permit any third party to: (a) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to discover the source code, object code, underlying structure, algorithms, or ideas of the Platform, except to the extent that such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law; (b) modify, translate, adapt, or create derivative works based upon the Platform or the Documentation; (c) sublicense, resell, rent, lease, lend, distribute, transfer, or otherwise make the Platform available to any third party, including through a service bureau, outsourcing arrangement, or time-sharing arrangement; (d) access or use the Platform in excess of the number of Authorized Users or authorized locations specified in the Order Form; (e) remove, alter, or obscure any proprietary notices, labels, or marks on the Platform or Documentation; (f) use the Platform in any manner that violates applicable law, regulation, or governmental order, including without limitation any applicable healthcare privacy laws or regulations; (g) use the Platform to store or transmit any Virus or other malicious code; (h) interfere with or disrupt the integrity or performance of the Platform or the systems or networks used to deliver the Platform; (i) access the Platform for purposes of building a competitive product or service, or for purposes of benchmarking or competitive analysis; or (j) use the Platform in a manner that exceeds the scope of the rights expressly granted under this Agreement.

**2.3 Subprocessors.** Vaultline may engage Subprocessors in connection with the provision of the Platform and related services. As of the Effective Date, Vaultline\'s Subprocessors include Amazon Web Services, Inc. (hosting and infrastructure services, with Customer Data hosted in the us-east-1 and us-west-2 regions). Vaultline shall maintain a current list of its Subprocessors, which shall be made available to Customer upon written request. Vaultline shall provide Customer with written notice of any material changes to its Subprocessor list, including the addition of new Subprocessors, at least thirty (30) days prior to the effective date of such change. Vaultline shall remain responsible for the acts and omissions of its Subprocessors to the same extent as if such acts or omissions were performed by Vaultline directly.

**2.4 Customer Responsibilities.** Customer shall be responsible for: (a) ensuring that all Authorized Users comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Documentation; (b) maintaining the confidentiality and security of all login credentials, passwords, and access tokens issued to Authorized Users, and promptly notifying Vaultline of any unauthorized use of such credentials; (c) providing accurate and complete information as reasonably requested by Vaultline for configuration, implementation, and ongoing operation of the Platform; (d) ensuring that Customer\'s systems, networks, and internet connectivity meet the minimum technical requirements specified in the Documentation and are compatible with the Platform; (e) obtaining and maintaining all necessary consents, authorizations, and permissions required under applicable law for the collection, processing, and transmission of Customer Data through the Platform; and (f) designating a primary point of contact to serve as the liaison between Customer and Vaultline for purposes of this Agreement.

**2.5 Reservation of Rights.** Except for the limited access rights expressly granted in Section 2.1, no other rights are granted to Customer under this Agreement, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. All rights not expressly granted herein are reserved by Vaultline.

**[SECTION 3: FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**3.1 Fees.** Customer shall pay the Fees as set forth in the Order Form (Exhibit A). The Fees include: (a) the Annual Subscription Fee for access to and use of the Platform during each Contract Year; and (b) the one-time Implementation Fee for the Implementation Services described in Section 4. Unless otherwise specified in a separately executed statement of work, all Fees for Professional Services shall be set forth in the applicable statement of work or change order and shall be in addition to the Fees set forth in the Order Form. All Fee escalation provisions are set forth in Section 3.3 below.

**3.2 Payment Terms.** All Fees shall be invoiced and payable as follows:

> \(a\) The Implementation Fee shall be invoiced upon execution of this Agreement and shall be due and payable within fifteen (15) days of the date of invoice.
>
> \(b\) Annual Subscription Fees shall be invoiced on the Effective Date for the first Contract Year and on each anniversary of the Effective Date thereafter, and shall be due and payable within fifteen (15) days of the date of invoice. For the avoidance of doubt, Annual Subscription Fees are payable in full annually in advance.
>
> \(c\) All Fees shall be paid in United States dollars by wire transfer or ACH payment to the account designated by Vaultline in the applicable invoice.
>
> \(d\) If any undisputed amount is not received by Vaultline by the due date, such overdue amount shall bear interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, calculated from the due date until the date of actual payment.
>
> \(e\) Customer shall be responsible for all sales, use, value-added, goods and services, withholding, and other taxes, duties, and governmental assessments of any nature imposed in connection with the Fees or this Agreement, other than taxes based solely on Vaultline\'s net income. If Customer is required by law to withhold or deduct any taxes from payments to Vaultline, Customer shall gross up the payment so that Vaultline receives the full amount of the Fees as if no withholding or deduction had been made.

**3.3 Fee Escalation.** Commencing on the first anniversary of the Effective Date, and on each anniversary thereafter during the Term (including any Renewal Term), the Annual Subscription Fee shall increase by the greater of (i) five percent (5%) or (ii) the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. City Average, as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the twelve (12)-month period ending on the most recently available date prior to such anniversary. For the avoidance of doubt, in no event shall the Annual Subscription Fee decrease from one Contract Year to the next as a result of this provision.

**3.4 Disputed Invoices.** If Customer in good faith disputes any portion of an invoice, Customer shall provide Vaultline with written notice of such dispute within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the invoice, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute and the disputed amount. Customer shall pay all undisputed amounts in accordance with the payment terms set forth in Section 3.2. The parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve any disputed amounts within thirty (30) days of Vaultline\'s receipt of Customer\'s dispute notice. Vaultline shall not suspend or terminate Customer\'s access to the Platform solely on account of amounts that are the subject of a good-faith dispute, provided that Customer has paid all undisputed amounts when due.

**3.5 Suspension for Non-Payment.** Without limiting its other rights and remedies under this Agreement, if any undisputed amount remains unpaid for more than thirty (30) days past its due date, Vaultline may, upon ten (10) days\' prior written notice to Customer, suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform until such overdue amount, together with all accrued interest, is paid in full. **4.2 Customer Cooperation.** Customer acknowledges that the successful and timely completion of the Implementation Services depends on Customer\'s reasonable cooperation and assistance. Customer shall: (a) designate a project manager to serve as the primary point of contact for the implementation and to coordinate Customer\'s internal resources; (b) provide Vaultline with timely access to Customer\'s systems, networks, and facilities as reasonably necessary for the Implementation Services; (c) provide Vaultline with accurate and complete data, credentials, and system specifications as reasonably requested; (d) make Customer personnel reasonably available for meetings, testing, feedback, and training sessions; and (e) promptly review and respond to Vaultline\'s requests for information, decisions, and approvals. If Customer fails to deliver a Non-Conformity Notice within the applicable acceptance period, the Platform shall be deemed accepted. Standard support services are included in the Annual Subscription Fee, and no separate support fees shall be charged for standard-tier support during the Term. **5.4 Planned Maintenance.** Vaultline shall perform routine planned maintenance on the Platform and its underlying infrastructure as necessary to ensure the continued performance, security, and stability of the Platform. Vaultline shall endeavor to schedule planned maintenance during non-business hours and shall provide Customer with reasonable advance notice of any planned maintenance that may materially affect Customer\'s use of the Platform. The Uptime Commitment shall apply commencing on the first day of the first full calendar month following the Deployment Date (as defined in Section 4.3 of the Agreement).

**B.2 Definitions.** For purposes of this SLA, the following definitions shall apply:

**\"Monthly Uptime Percentage\"** means the total number of minutes in a calendar month, minus the number of minutes of Downtime during such calendar month, divided by the total number of minutes in such calendar month, expressed as a percentage. The formula is as follows:

Monthly Uptime Percentage = ((Total Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100

**\"Downtime\"** means any period during which the Platform is materially unavailable or materially impaired such that Customer\'s Authorized Users are unable to access or use the core functionality of the Platform, as measured by Vaultline\'s monitoring systems. Downtime shall not include any period of unavailability or impairment resulting from:

> \(a\) Scheduled maintenance windows of up to eight (8) hours per week, which Vaultline shall endeavor to schedule during non-business hours (between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM Central Time) but is not obligated to do so;
>
> \(b\) Downtime resulting from Customer\'s equipment, software, internet connectivity, or other systems or infrastructure not provided by Vaultline;
>
> \(c\) Downtime caused by Force Majeure Events as defined in Section 14.4 of the Agreement;
>
> \(d\) Downtime resulting from Customer\'s actions or inactions, including any changes to Customer\'s configurations, unauthorized modifications, or failure to implement recommended updates; or
>
> \(e\) Downtime resulting from features or functionality designated by Vaultline as \"beta,\" \"preview,\" or \"experimental.\"

**B.3 Service Credits**

In the event that the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below the Uptime Commitment in any calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive a service credit equal to two percent (2%) of the monthly Subscription Fee for each full one percent (1%) by which the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below the Uptime Commitment in the applicable month (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). For purposes of calculating Service Credits, the monthly Subscription Fee shall be the Annual Subscription Fee divided by twelve (12). Service Credits shall be Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Vaultline to meet the Uptime Commitment.

**Claiming Service Credits.** To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vaultline within fifteen (15) business days following the end of the calendar month in which the Uptime Commitment was not met. The request must include: (i) the dates and times of the claimed Downtime; (ii) a description of the impact on Customer\'s use of the Platform; and (iii) any documentation or log files supporting Customer\'s claim. Vaultline shall review the request and, if the claim is verified by Vaultline\'s monitoring systems, shall apply the Service Credit to Customer\'s next invoice. In the event of a discrepancy between Customer\'s records and Vaultline\'s monitoring systems, Vaultline\'s monitoring systems shall control. Service Credits are not redeemable for cash and may not be transferred or applied to any other account or agreement.

**B.4 Maximum Service Credits**

In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed ten percent (10%) of the monthly Subscription Fee for such month. Service Credits shall not be cumulative from one month to the next. Any unused or unclaimed Service Credits shall expire at the end of the calendar month following the month in which they were earned.

**B.5 Sole Remedy**

The Service Credits set forth in this Exhibit B shall constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vaultline\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any failure by Vaultline to meet the Uptime Commitment or any other service level target set forth in this SLA. Nothing in this SLA shall be construed to limit or modify the limitation of liability provisions set forth in Section 12 of the Agreement.

**B.6 Platform Support**

During the Term, Vaultline shall provide support for the Platform through the following channels:

> • **Email Support:** support@vaultlinesoftware.com
>
> • **Web Portal:** Vaultline\'s customer support portal at support.vaultlinesoftware.com

Standard support is available during Support Hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM Central Time, excluding Vaultline-observed holidays). Phone support is not included in the standard support tier. Customer may purchase enhanced support tiers, including 24/7 phone support, at additional cost as agreed by the parties in writing.

**Response Time Targets.** Vaultline shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to support requests within the following target timeframes. These response time targets are informational guidelines and are not binding commitments or warranties. Failure to meet these targets shall not constitute a breach of this Agreement.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Severity Level**        **Description**                                                                                                 **Target Initial Response Time**
  ------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------
  Severity 1 --- Critical   Platform is completely unavailable or a critical business function is inoperable with no workaround available   2 hours during Support Hours

  Severity 2 --- High       A major feature or function of the Platform is significantly impaired with no practical workaround              4 hours during Support Hours

  Severity 3 --- Medium     A minor feature or function is impaired, but a workaround is available; limited business impact                 1 business day

  Severity 4 --- Low        General questions, informational requests, or minor cosmetic issues with no material business impact            2 business days
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Severity levels shall be assigned by Vaultline based on the information provided by Customer at the time of the support request. Vaultline may reclassify the severity level of a support request based on its assessment of the actual impact and urgency.

**--- END OF EXHIBIT B ---**

**LIST OF EXHIBITS**

The following Exhibits are attached to and incorporated into the Master Software-as-a-Service Agreement:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Exhibit**                         **Title**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Exhibit A                           Order Form

  Exhibit B                           Service Level Agreement
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

*\[End of Agreement\]*

/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/review-enterprise-saas-agreement-against-company-playbook/claude-code-session/20261016-040042 'mkdir -p /workspace/build && cat > /workspace/build/content1.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
# Issue content: each issue dict
ISSUES = []
def I(**k): ISSUES.append(k)

I(no="1", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Business Associate Agreement deferred; no BAA attached",
 msa="MSA \u00a7 7.5; \u00a7 1.4; \u00a7 14.6; Exhibit list (Exhibits A and B only)",
 pb="Playbook \u00a7 7.1 (Required); App. B (Ridgecrest)",
 provision="Section 7.5 states only that a BAA \u201cmay be required\u201d and that the parties \u201cshall negotiate in good faith to execute a BAA within ninety (90) days of the Effective Date.\u201d No BAA is attached; Section 14.6 refers to \u201cany subsequently executed Business Associate Agreement.\u201d",
 position="A BAA conforming to 45 CFR \u00a7\u00a7 164.502(e) and 164.504(e) must be fully executed as a condition precedent to the earlier of the Effective Date or any PHI transfer, attached as an exhibit or signed simultaneously. \u201cNegotiate in good faith\u201d / deferred BAA language must be rejected. Panorama form BAA preferred. Ridgecrest: deferred BAA execution is not acceptable.",
 gap="Direct deviation from a non-negotiable Required position and a Ridgecrest mandate. The draft does not even concede that Vaultline is a business associate. The timing makes the gap acute: under Order Form Exhibit A, implementation begins within 10 business days of November 1, 2024, with MedBridge EHR integration by December 31, 2024 and data migration by January 15, 2025 \u2014 i.e., PHI from ~2.3 million annual encounters would flow to Vaultline (and its Subprocessor AWS) well before the 90-day window (January 30, 2025) closes, and an \u201cagreement to negotiate\u201d is likely unenforceable in any event.",
 risk="Critical. Disclosure of PHI to a business associate without a compliant BAA is a direct HIPAA Privacy/Security Rule violation by Panorama as covered entity (civil monetary penalty exposure, OCR corrective action plan), and a Ridgecrest compliance failure.",
 rec="Reject \u00a7 7.5. Make execution of Panorama\u2019s form BAA (attached as Exhibit C) a condition precedent to the Effective Date and to any PHI access. Order of precedence: BAA controls. If Vaultline insists on its own BAA form, Legal must review it against Playbook \u00a7 7 and Appendix B before signature; do not sign the MSA without the BAA. If the BAA cannot be finalized by November 1, move the Effective Date (and the fee start) rather than defer the BAA.",
 redline="Replace Section 7.5 with: \u201c7.5 Business Associate Agreement. Vaultline acknowledges that it will create, receive, maintain, and transmit Protected Health Information on behalf of Customer and is a \u2018business associate\u2019 of Customer as defined at 45 CFR \u00a7 160.103. Concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, the parties shall execute the Business Associate Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit C (the \u2018BAA\u2019). Execution of the BAA by both parties is a condition precedent to the effectiveness of this Agreement and to any access to, or transfer or disclosure of, Protected Health Information to Vaultline or any Subprocessor. In the event of any conflict between the BAA and this Agreement, the BAA shall control.\u201d Conform \u00a7 1.4 and \u00a7 14.6 (delete \u201cany subsequently executed\u201d) and add Exhibit C to the List of Exhibits.",
 fallback="None. This is a non-negotiable Required position (no GC deviation should be sought). The only flexibility is the BAA form (Vaultline paper acceptable if it meets Playbook \u00a7 7 and App. B).",
 approval="No deviation permitted.")

I(no="2", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Vendor ownership and commercial sale of \u201cAggregated De-Identified Data\u201d; non-HIPAA de-identification standard",
 msa="MSA \u00a7 6.3; \u00a7 1.2; \u00a7 11.5(d) (Section 6 survives)",
 pb="Playbook \u00a7 6.1 (Required: Aggregated and De-Identified Data; Preferred: no derivative rights)",
 provision="Notwithstanding Customer ownership in \u00a7 6.2, \u00a7 6.3 gives Vaultline ownership of all Aggregated De-Identified Data, the right to use it \u201cfor any lawful purpose, including \u2026 research, and commercial sale to third parties,\u201d and an affirmative assignment from Customer with a further-assurances covenant. \u201cDe-identified\u201d is defined only as data that \u201cdoes not identify Customer or any individual.\u201d The right survives termination (\u00a7 11.5(d)).",
 position="Any vendor use of de-identified data requires: (a) HIPAA de-identification under Safe Harbor (45 CFR \u00a7 164.514(b)) or Expert Determination (\u00a7 164.514(a)), with the method specified; (b) no re-identification of Customer, any patient, individual, or facility, and no re-identification attempts; (c) use limited to internal product improvement and internal benchmarking \u2014 no sale, licensing, or distribution to third parties without Customer\u2019s prior written consent in its sole discretion; (d) BAA addresses the methodology and Customer has audit rights over the de-identification process. Preferred: no vendor rights in derivatives at all.",
 gap="Fails all four Required conditions. The generic \u201cdoes not identify\u201d standard is exactly the formulation the Playbook rejects; the definition does not protect against identification of Panorama facilities or re-identification; commercial sale is expressly permitted; ownership is transferred (not licensed) and is perpetual; there is no BAA and no audit right. Note also the asymmetry with \u00a7 2.2(i), which prohibits Panorama from using the Platform for benchmarking while Vaultline may sell benchmarks built from Panorama data.",
 risk="Critical. The creation of de-identified data from PHI is itself a use of PHI that must be permitted by the BAA; data that is not de-identified to the HIPAA standard remains PHI, and its sale would be an impermissible disclosure/sale of PHI (45 CFR \u00a7 164.502(a)(5)(ii)). Reputational exposure across 14 clinics; competitive exposure if datasets reach competitors or an acquirer.",
 rec="Open with the Preferred position: delete \u00a7 6.3 and \u00a7 1.2 entirely. Fallback (Required minimum): non-exclusive, revocable license (no assignment, no Vaultline ownership) to HIPAA-de-identified data, internal product improvement/benchmarking only, no third-party sale/licensing, no re-identification, method specified, audit right, terminates with the Agreement, and covered by the BAA.",
 redline="Delete Section 1.2 and replace Section 6.3 with: \u201c6.3 De-Identified Data. Vaultline shall not de-identify, aggregate, or create derivatives of Customer Data except as expressly permitted in this Section 6.3. Subject to the BAA, Customer grants Vaultline a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license during the Term to create data de-identified in accordance with [the Safe Harbor method at 45 CFR \u00a7 164.514(b)(2)] [the Expert Determination method at 45 CFR \u00a7 164.514(b)(1)] (\u2018De-Identified Data\u2019), and to use De-Identified Data solely for Vaultline\u2019s internal product improvement and internal benchmarking. De-Identified Data shall not identify, and shall not be reasonably capable of being used to re-identify, Customer, any Customer facility, any patient, or any other individual. Vaultline shall not (a) attempt to re-identify any De-Identified Data, or (b) sell, license, disclose, or otherwise make available De-Identified Data or any data set or output derived therefrom to any third party without Customer\u2019s prior written consent, which Customer may withhold in its sole discretion. Customer may audit Vaultline\u2019s de-identification processes in accordance with Section 7.8. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title, and interest in De-Identified Data; nothing herein assigns any right to Vaultline.\u201d",
 fallback="Fallback is the Required minimum above. Any broader right (e.g., third-party research use) would be a deviation from a Required position requiring GC approval and should not be offered.",
 approval="GC approval required for any deviation from the four Required conditions.")

I(no="3", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Security commitments limited to \u201ccommercially reasonable\u201d safeguards; no SOC 2 Type II; no audit rights",
 msa="MSA \u00a7 7.2 (no audit or SOC 2 provision anywhere in the MSA)",
 pb="Playbook \u00a7 7.2 (Required: SOC 2 Type II; Audit Rights; Specific Security Commitments; Ridgecrest Requirement); App. B",
 provision="Section 7.2 commits Vaultline only to \u201ccommercially reasonable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to\u201d protect Customer Data, with periodic review. There is no SOC 2 Type II obligation, no reporting of audit results, and no Customer audit right. The SLA also provides no right to audit uptime data (see Issue 12).",
 position="Vendor must maintain current SOC 2 Type II covering Security, Availability, and Confidentiality; provide the latest report on request, annually, and within 30 days of issuance. Customer audit right (itself or a qualified independent third party), at Customer\u2019s expense, on 30 days\u2019 notice, once per year plus after a Security Incident/breach/reasonable suspicion; full cooperation; no separate NDA condition. Specific safeguards consistent with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C) and NIST CSF \u2014 not \u201ccommercially reasonable\u201d or \u201cindustry standard.\u201d Ridgecrest: SOC 2 Type II non-negotiable for PHI vendors.",
 gap="All three Required elements are missing (confirming the GC\u2019s preliminary read). We also do not know whether Vaultline currently holds a SOC 2 Type II report; if it does not, the Playbook treats that as a material deviation that may warrant rejection of a Tier 1 engagement.",
 risk="Critical. Vague standards give no measurable baseline for breach claims; inability to verify controls for a platform holding high-volume PHI on AWS with cross-cloud flows from Panorama\u2019s Azure environment; Ridgecrest non-compliance reportable in the quarterly report.",
 rec="Request Vaultline\u2019s current SOC 2 Type II report (and bridge letter) immediately, before the October 14 call if possible. Insert a new security exhibit and the provisions below. Add encryption in transit and at rest for the Azure-to-AWS data flows Derek identified.",
 redline="Replace Section 7.2 and add Sections 7.7\u20137.8: \u201c7.2 Security Program. Vaultline shall implement and maintain a written information security program with administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that (a) comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C) and (b) are consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, including, at a minimum, encryption of Customer Data in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher, including all data flows between Customer\u2019s Microsoft Azure environment and the Platform) and at rest (AES-256 or equivalent), multi-factor authentication for administrative access, role-based access controls, logging and monitoring, vulnerability management and annual third-party penetration testing, and tested backup and disaster recovery. 7.7 SOC 2. Vaultline shall maintain throughout the Term a current SOC 2 Type II report covering, at a minimum, the Security, Availability, and Confidentiality trust services criteria, and shall deliver the most recent report to Customer upon execution, upon request, and within thirty (30) days after issuance of each new report. Vaultline shall promptly remediate any exceptions noted. 7.8 Audit. Upon not less than thirty (30) days\u2019 prior written notice, Customer or a qualified independent third party designated by Customer may, at Customer\u2019s expense and not more than once per calendar year (provided that additional audits may be conducted following a Security Incident or where Customer reasonably suspects non-compliance), audit Vaultline\u2019s security practices, data handling procedures, physical and logical access controls, de-identification processes, and compliance with this Agreement and the BAA. Vaultline shall cooperate fully and provide timely access to relevant records, personnel, and systems. No audit shall be conditioned on any confidentiality agreement other than Section 8.\u201d",
 fallback="Customer may accept that the annual audit is satisfied in the first instance by the SOC 2 Type II report plus a security questionnaire, provided the on-site/third-party audit right remains available after a Security Incident or reasonable suspicion of non-compliance. SOC 2 Type II itself has no fallback (Ridgecrest).",
 approval="SOC 2 Type II: no deviation (report any to Ridgecrest). Audit-right modifications: GC approval.")

I(no="4", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Security Incident notice: 72 hours from \u201cconfirmation\u201d; incomplete content; no cost allocation",
 msa="MSA \u00a7 7.3; \u00a7 1.16",
 pb="Playbook \u00a7 7.3 (Required: timeline, content, cooperation and cost; Preferred: 12 hours, vendor bears all costs)",
 provision="Notice within 72 hours \u201cof confirming the occurrence\u201d of a Security Incident. Content omits whether PHI is involved/specific data elements and a designated vendor point of contact. Vaultline must \u201ccooperate,\u201d but bears no notification, credit-monitoring, forensic, or regulatory costs. \u201cSecurity Incident\u201d (\u00a7 1.16) omits \u201cdestruction\u201d of Customer Data.",
 position="Notice within 24 hours of discovery, or of when Vaultline knew or reasonably should have known \u2014 triggered by discovery or reasonable belief, not confirmation. Content: nature/scope incl. categories and number of records; specific data elements incl. PHI; corrective actions; named point of contact; ongoing supplemental reports. Vendor bears notification, credit monitoring, forensics, regulatory response and remediation costs to the extent caused by its acts/omissions. Definition must include destruction. Preferred: 12 hours; vendor bears all costs regardless of fault.",
 gap="Clock is 3x longer and starts at the wrong trigger (the \u201cconfirmation\u201d standard the Playbook specifically rejects), so the effective delay is open-ended. Missing content elements and cost allocation. Definition gap on destruction (e.g., ransomware wiping data).",
 risk="Critical. Panorama\u2019s own HIPAA breach-notification clock (45 CFR \u00a7 164.404, 60 days from discovery, with discovery imputed when a business associate agent knows) and state-law clocks can run while Vaultline is still \u201cconfirming.\u201d Costs of notifying patients from ~2.3 million annual encounters would fall on Panorama and, under \u00a7 12.2, may be unrecoverable as consequential damages.",
 rec="Open at Preferred (12 hours; vendor bears all costs). Accept no less than Required (24 hours from discovery/reasonable belief; fault-based cost allocation). Conform the BAA.",
 redline="Amend \u00a7 1.16 to add \u201cdestruction of, or loss of access to,\u201d after \u201cdisclosure of,\u201d and add \u201cwhether or not such event constitutes a \u2018breach\u2019 under HIPAA or state law.\u201d Replace the first sentence of \u00a7 7.3 with: \u201cVaultline shall notify Customer in writing without unreasonable delay and in no event later than [twelve (12)] [twenty-four (24)] hours after Vaultline discovers, or reasonably believes, that a Security Incident has occurred (or the time at which Vaultline knew or reasonably should have known of such Security Incident).\u201d Add to the content list: \u201c(e) the specific data elements affected, including whether Protected Health Information was involved; and (f) the name, title, and contact information of Vaultline\u2019s designated point of contact for the Security Incident.\u201d Add: \u201cTo the extent a Security Incident results from the acts or omissions of Vaultline or its Subprocessors or a breach of this Agreement or the BAA, Vaultline shall reimburse Customer for all reasonable costs of investigation, forensic analysis, notification of individuals, regulators and media as required by law, call-center support, credit and identity monitoring for affected individuals for not less than twenty-four (24) months, regulatory response, and other remediation. Such costs shall be deemed direct damages.\u201d",
 fallback="Required minimum: 24 hours from discovery/reasonable belief and fault-based cost allocation. No fallback beyond that.",
 approval="Any notice period >24 hours or confirmation trigger: GC approval (not recommended).")

I(no="5", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Liability cap of six months\u2019 fees \u201cactually paid\u201d; no uncapped carve-outs; unqualified consequential-damages waiver",
 msa="MSA \u00a7\u00a7 12.1\u201312.4; \u00a7 10.2 (sole remedy); Exhibit B \u00a7 B.5",
 pb="Playbook \u00a7 8.1 (Required: cap \u2265 2x trailing-12-month fees; uncapped categories; consequential carve-outs; Preferred: 3x and no waiver); \u00a7 16 (confidentiality carve-out)",
 provision="Mutual aggregate cap equal to fees \u201cactually paid by Customer \u2026 in the six (6)-month period immediately preceding the event.\u201d No exclusions from the cap. Mutual waiver of indirect, consequential, special, incidental and punitive damages and \u201cany loss of \u2026 data,\u201d with no carve-outs, applying even on failure of essential purpose.",
 position="Cap no less than 2x the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the event (minimum $2,280,000 on $1,140,000 annual fees; Preferred 3x = $3,420,000). Uncapped: (a) data protection/security/confidentiality breaches incl. Security Incidents; (b) IP indemnity; (c) confidentiality breach; (d) gross negligence/willful misconduct; (e) BAA obligations. Any consequential-damages waiver must carve out data breaches/Security Incidents, confidentiality breaches and IP indemnity.",
 gap="The cap is roughly one quarter of the Required minimum on its face (6 months of $1,140,000 = $570,000 vs. $2,280,000). Worse, because fees are payable annually in advance (\u00a7 3.2(b)) and the cap counts only fees \u201cactually paid\u201d in the prior six months, the cap would be approximately $0 for any claim arising roughly six months after each annual payment (e.g., an event in June\u2013October 2025, when no payment has been made since mid-November 2024), and up to $1,425,000 for an event shortly after the Year 1 payments. None of the five Required uncapped categories is carved out, and the consequential waiver expressly bars recovery of lost data and would capture breach-notification, credit-monitoring, forensic and regulatory costs.",
 risk="Critical. A material PHI breach involving data from ~2.3 million annual encounters could generate eight-figure costs; the draft effectively immunizes Vaultline from the harms most likely to result from its own breach, and limits the value of the IP indemnity.",
 rec="Open at Preferred: 3x trailing 12 months fees paid or payable; delete the consequential waiver or carve out all five categories. Required minimum: 2x with the five uncapped categories and three consequential carve-outs. Also strike \u201cactually paid\u201d and the six-month lookback, and carve the Customer\u2019s payment obligations out of the mutual cap only if Vaultline insists on symmetry.",
 redline="Replace \u00a7 12.1 with: \u201cEXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY\u2019S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED [THREE (3)] [TWO (2)] TIMES THE TOTAL FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM (OR, FOR CLAIMS ARISING IN THE FIRST CONTRACT YEAR, THE FEES PAYABLE FOR THE FIRST CONTRACT YEAR).\u201d Add \u00a7 12.5: \u201c\u2018Excluded Claims\u2019 means (a) Vaultline\u2019s breach of Section 7 (Data Protection and Security), Section 8 (Confidentiality), or the BAA, including any Security Incident; (b) Vaultline\u2019s indemnification obligations under Section 10.1; (c) a party\u2019s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct; and (d) Vaultline\u2019s obligations under the BAA. The limitations in Sections 12.1 and 12.2 shall not apply to Excluded Claims.\u201d Amend \u00a7 12.2 to begin \u201cEXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS,\u201d and delete \u201cDATA,\u201d from the list of excluded losses.",
 fallback="If Vaultline will not accept uncapped security exposure, a separate \u201csuper-cap\u201d for data-breach claims is a deviation from a Required position requiring GC approval; it should be no less than the $10,000,000 cyber/E&O insurance limit and paired with the Issue 6 insurance increase. IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct and BAA obligations should remain uncapped.",
 approval="Cap <2x or any super-cap in lieu of uncapped categories: GC approval with risk-assessment memorandum.")
EOF
echo ok'

input.command:
/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/review-enterprise-saas-agreement-against-company-playbook/claude-code-session/20261016-040042 'cat > /workspace/build/content2.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
from content1 import ISSUES, I

I(no="6", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="IP indemnity: combination carve-out negates coverage for the MedBridge EHR integration; Documentation carve-out; narrow scope",
 msa="MSA §§ 10.1, 10.2, 1.7; § 4.1(b); Exhibit A (Integration)",
 pb="Playbook § 8.2 (Required: Vendor IP Indemnity; No Carve-Outs for Authorized Use; Remediation; Preferred: full, uncapped, no carve-outs); § 8.1(b) (uncapped)",
 provision="Vaultline indemnifies Customer and its officers, directors, employees and agents (not Affiliates) only for claims that use of the Platform infringes a United States patent, copyright or trademark or misappropriates a trade secret, excluding claims arising from (i) unauthorized modification, (ii) “Customer’s combination of the Platform with any products, services, data, or technology not provided by Vaultline,” or (iii) use other than in accordance with the Documentation. Remedies in § 10.2 are at Vaultline’s option (“may”), and §§ 10.1–10.2 are the “sole and exclusive remedy” for IP Claims. The indemnity is subject to the six-month cap (Issue 5).",
 position="Indemnity must cover Customer and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees and agents against claims that authorized use infringes or misappropriates any third-party IP right (patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, other proprietary rights). No carve-out may negate coverage for contemplated use; a combination carve-out is unacceptable where the platform is designed to integrate with third-party systems such as MedBridge EHR; a Documentation carve-out is acceptable only if the Documentation fully reflects the contracted use and integrations. Remediation must be mandatory (procure, modify, or terminate with pro-rata refund). IP indemnity must be uncapped.",
 gap="The combination carve-out squarely captures the deal’s core use case. Per Derek, “the entire value proposition depends on Prism pulling data from MedBridge,” and under § 4.1(b) and the Order Form Vaultline itself builds the MedBridge interfaces using its “standard EHR connector module” — yet MedBridge EHR and Customer Data are “not provided by Vaultline,” so virtually any claim involving the integrated workflow could be excluded, rendering the indemnity illusory. The Documentation carve-out is tied to Vaultline’s generic Documentation “as updated by Vaultline from time to time” (§ 1.7), which does not describe Panorama’s integration and can be changed unilaterally. Coverage is US-only and excludes other proprietary rights; affiliates are not indemnitees; remediation is permissive; the indemnity is capped.",
 risk="Critical (IP). Analytics/EHR-interoperability software is a frequent target of patent assertion. Without coverage for the integrated use, Panorama would bear defense costs and damages and could face injunction risk for a platform it does not control. Given the IP complexity, consider involving Thornfield & Associates if Vaultline resists (Playbook § 3).",
 rec="Insist on full coverage for the contracted use including the MedBridge integration, Vaultline-provided connectors, and Customer Data as processed by the Platform. Limit the combination exclusion to combinations not provided, specified, recommended, or reasonably contemplated by Vaultline. Tie the Documentation exclusion to a fixed SOW/Documentation version that expressly describes the MedBridge integration. Make remediation mandatory and uncapped.",
 redline="Amend § 10.1: replace “officers, directors, employees, agents” with “Affiliates, and its and their officers, directors, employees, agents”; replace “infringes any United States patent, copyright, or trademark, or misappropriates any trade secret” with “infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property or proprietary right of a third party”; and replace exclusions (ii) and (iii) with: “(ii) the combination of the Platform with products, services, or technology not provided by Vaultline, where the claim would not have arisen but for such combination; provided that this clause (ii) shall not apply to any combination that is provided, specified, recommended, enabled, or approved by Vaultline or reasonably contemplated by this Agreement, the Order Form, any SOW, or the Documentation, including the integration of the Platform with MedBridge EHR and any other Customer system identified in the Order Form or SOW, Vaultline’s EHR connector modules, and the processing of Customer Data by the Platform; or (iii) Customer’s use of the Platform in material breach of this Agreement, provided that use in accordance with the Order Form, any SOW, or the Documentation as in effect on the Effective Date (which the parties agree accurately describes Customer’s contemplated use, including the MedBridge integration) shall not be excluded.” In § 10.2 replace “may, at its sole option” with “shall, at its option” and conform the refund to “prepaid, unused Fees calculated on a daily pro-rata basis, together with any unperformed Implementation Fees, within thirty (30) days.” Delete the “sole and exclusive remedy” sentence or limit it to the remedies for continued use. Add § 10.1 to the Excluded Claims in § 12.5.",
 fallback="A documentation carve-out may stay if the Documentation (or an SOW exhibit) as of the Effective Date is frozen for indemnity purposes and specifically describes the MedBridge integration. A combination carve-out limited to genuinely uncontemplated third-party combinations is acceptable. Capping IP indemnity is a deviation from a Required position (GC approval).",
 approval="Any carve-out that reaches the MedBridge integration or any cap on IP indemnity: GC approval (not recommended).")

I(no="7", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Cyber insurance $5M (vs. $10M); no Technology E&O; 12-month tail; no additional insured; certificates only on request",
 msa="MSA §§ 13.1(c), 13.2; § 11.5(d)",
 pb="Playbook § 9 (Required: $10M combined cyber + Tech E&O; coverages (a)–(e); additional insured/waiver of subrogation; COI on execution and annually; 30-day notice; 2-year tail; Preferred: $15M, A.M. Best A-); App. B (Ridgecrest $10M)",
 provision="Cyber liability of $5,000,000 per claim and aggregate (network security, privacy, breach notification, regulatory defense and penalties, media) from “Clearpoint Cyber Underwriters or a carrier of comparable financial strength”; CGL $2M/$4M; workers’ comp/employer’s liability. Coverage for 12 months post-term. Primary and non-contributory; 30-day notice of change. Certificates only “upon Customer’s written request.”",
 position="Combined cyber + technology E&O of at least $10,000,000 per occurrence and aggregate covering items (a)–(e) including tech E&O; Panorama as additional insured (or waiver of subrogation); COI at execution and annually on the anniversary; 30 days’ notice; maintained through the Term plus 2 years. Preferred: $15M; A.M. Best A- or better.",
 gap="Limit is 50% of the Required (and Ridgecrest-mandated) minimum; Technology E&O is absent entirely (so failure-to-perform claims are uninsured); tail is 12 months vs. 2 years; no additional insured/waiver of subrogation; COI only on request. No carrier rating standard — we have no information on Clearpoint Cyber Underwriters’ A.M. Best rating, which should be verified. Also, § 13 survives only “solely with respect to claims arising during the Term,” which undercuts the tail.",
 risk="Critical (Sponsor). $5M is thin relative to breach exposure for this PHI volume and the Liability position in Issue 5; must be flagged in the Ridgecrest quarterly compliance report if not cured.",
 rec="Require $10M combined cyber + tech E&O (open at $15M with A- rating), additional insured status, COI at signing and annually, and 2-year tail. Add failure to maintain insurance as an immediate termination event (Issue 15).",
 redline="Replace § 13.1(c) with: “(c) Cyber Liability and Technology Errors and Omissions Insurance, with combined limits of not less than [Fifteen] [Ten] Million Dollars ($[15,000,000] [10,000,000]) per occurrence/claim and in the aggregate, covering (i) network security and privacy liability, including unauthorized access to or acquisition, use, disclosure, or destruction of personally identifiable information and Protected Health Information; (ii) data breach response and notification costs, including individual notification, substitute notice, call-center services, credit monitoring, and identity theft insurance; (iii) regulatory defense costs, fines, penalties, and assessments to the extent insurable by law; (iv) media liability; and (v) technology errors and omissions.” Amend the lead-in to read “During the Term and for a period of two (2) years following the expiration or termination” and add: “All insurers shall have an A.M. Best rating of A- (VIII) or better. Vaultline shall cause Panorama Health Systems, Inc. to be named as an additional insured on the policy required by Section 13.1(c) or, if the carrier’s form does not permit, shall provide a waiver of subrogation in favor of Customer.” Replace § 13.2 first sentence: “Vaultline shall deliver certificates of insurance evidencing the required coverage upon execution of this Agreement and annually on each anniversary of the Effective Date.” Amend § 11.5(d) to delete “solely with respect to claims arising during the Term.”",
 fallback="If Vaultline cannot place a single $10M tower immediately, accept separate cyber and tech E&O policies that together equal $10M, with confirmation of a binder before the Effective Date. No fallback below $10M (Ridgecrest).",
 approval="Below $10M: not approvable without Ridgecrest reporting; GC approval required for any other deviation.")

I(no="8", pri="P1 - Critical", cat="A", title="Data return limited to 30-day self-service download; permissive deletion; no destruction certification",
 msa="MSA § 11.6; § 11.5(a); § 8.4",
 pb="Playbook § 6.2 (Required: Data Return; Data Destruction; Retention Exception; Preferred: Customer format, vendor bears costs); App. B (Ridgecrest)",
 provision="Upon termination Vaultline will “make Customer Data available for download through the Platform” for 30 days; afterwards Vaultline “may delete” Customer Data and has no liability for data not downloaded. No format, migration assistance, destruction obligation, NIST standard, or officer certification. Section 11.5(a) simultaneously provides that Customer’s access to the Platform ceases on termination, creating an internal conflict with the download right. Section 8.4 allows retention “as automatically retained in electronic backup or archival systems.”",
 position="Vendor must return all Customer Data within 30 days in a commercially standard machine-readable format (CSV, JSON, XML, SQL) specified by Customer, with reasonable migration assistance at no cost or a fixed/capped cost; then mandatorily destroy all copies (including subprocessors/hosting providers, i.e., AWS) within the later of 60 days after termination or 30 days after completing return, using NIST SP 800-88 methods, with written certification signed by an officer. Retention only as strictly required by law, with notice and continued protection.",
 gap="The draft shifts the entire burden of retrieval to Panorama, specifies no format, and uses the very “may delete” permissive language the Playbook prohibits. There is no destruction obligation or certification, and backups are carved out indefinitely. Section 11.5(a) may defeat even the 30-day download right.",
 risk="Critical (Sponsor). Loss of clinical analytics history at exit; PHI lingering in Vaultline/AWS backups after termination; Ridgecrest flags this as critical for any future exit or portfolio-company sale.",
 rec="Replace § 11.6 with full return-and-destroy mechanics; conform § 11.5(a) to preserve access/transition during the return period; narrow the § 8.4 backup exception to legally required retention with notice and destruction on the backup rotation cycle.",
 redline="Replace § 11.6 with: “11.6 Data Return and Destruction. (a) Within thirty (30) days after the effective date of expiration or termination for any reason, Vaultline shall return all Customer Data to Customer in a commercially standard, non-proprietary, machine-readable format (such as CSV, JSON, XML, or SQL database export) reasonably specified by Customer, and shall provide reasonable data-migration assistance at no additional charge. (b) Within the later of sixty (60) days after the effective date of expiration or termination or thirty (30) days after completion of the return under Section 11.6(a), Vaultline shall, and shall cause its Subprocessors to, permanently and irreversibly destroy all copies of Customer Data in their possession or control, including backups, using methods consistent with NIST Special Publication 800-88, and shall deliver to Customer a written certification of destruction signed by an officer of Vaultline. (c) Vaultline may retain Customer Data only to the extent strictly required by applicable law, shall promptly notify Customer of the legal basis, scope, and expected duration of such retention, and shall continue to protect retained Customer Data in accordance with Sections 7 and 8 and the BAA until destroyed.” Amend § 11.5(a) to add “except as necessary to perform Section 11.6.” Amend § 8.4 to provide that Customer Data is governed exclusively by § 11.6.",
 fallback="If Vaultline seeks a fee for migration assistance beyond the standard export, accept only a fixed or capped fee stated in the Order Form (Required). Core return/destruction/certification terms have no fallback (Ridgecrest).",
 approval="No deviation on return/destruction/certification (Ridgecrest).")

 redline="Replace the proviso in § 14.3 with: “Vaultline shall not assign, delegate, or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder, whether voluntarily, by operation of law, or in connection with any merger, consolidation, acquisition, reorganization, change of control, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity, without Customer’s prior written consent, which Customer may withhold in its reasonable discretion. Vaultline shall provide Customer written notice of any Change of Control within ten (10) days after its announcement.  fallback="Consent right with no CoC carve-out is Required/Ridgecrest (no fallback). The CoC termination right (Preferred) can be traded, e.g., limited to CoC by a competitor of Customer or followed by material product changes, if needed to secure the consent right and escrow.",

 provision="Vaultline indemnifies Customer and its officers, directors, employees and agents (not Affiliates) only for claims that use of the Platform infringes a United States patent, copyright or trademark or misappropriates a trade secret, excluding claims arising from (i) unauthorized modification, (ii) \u201cCustomer\u2019s combination of the Platform with any products, services, data, or technology not provided by Vaultline,\u201d or (iii) use other than in accordance with the Documentation.  position="Indemnity must cover Customer and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees and agents against claims that authorized use infringes or misappropriates any third-party IP right (patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, other proprietary rights).  gap="The combination carve-out squarely captures the deal\u2019s core use case.  risk="Critical (IP). Analytics/EHR-interoperability software is a frequent target of patent assertion.  rec="Insist on full coverage for the contracted use including the MedBridge integration, Vaultline-provided connectors, and Customer Data as processed by the Platform.  redline="Amend \u00a7 10.1: replace \u201cofficers, directors, employees, agents\u201d with \u201cAffiliates, and its and their officers, directors, employees, agents\u201d; replace \u201cinfringes any United States patent, copyright, or trademark, or misappropriates any trade secret\u201d with \u201cinfringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other intellectual property or proprietary right of a third party\u201d; and replace exclusions (ii) and (iii) with: \u201c(ii) the combination of the Platform with products, services, or technology not provided by Vaultline, where the claim would not have arisen but for such combination; provided that this clause (ii) shall not apply to any combination that is provided, specified, recommended, enabled, or approved by Vaultline or reasonably contemplated by this Agreement, the Order Form, any SOW, or the Documentation, including the integration of the Platform with MedBridge EHR and any other Customer system identified in the Order Form or SOW, Vaultline\u2019s EHR connector modules, and the processing of Customer Data by the Platform; or (iii) Customer\u2019s use of the Platform in material breach of this Agreement, provided that use in accordance with the Order Form, any SOW, or the Documentation as in effect on the Effective Date (which the parties agree accurately describes Customer\u2019s contemplated use, including the MedBridge integration) shall not be excluded.\u201d In \u00a7 10.2 replace \u201cmay, at its sole option\u201d with \u201cshall, at its option\u201d and conform the refund to \u201cprepaid, unused Fees calculated on a daily pro-rata basis, together with any unperformed Implementation Fees, within thirty (30) days.\u201d Delete the \u201csole and exclusive remedy\u201d sentence or limit it to the remedies for continued use. Bottom line: the Vaultline draft is a vendor-favorable form that is not executable in its current form. Measured against the Panorama SaaS Contracting Playbook (v3.2, last updated March 15, 2024), it deviates from Required positions in every major risk area the Playbook covers, and it fails five of the six Ridgecrest Capital Partners vendor-management requirements that apply to a PHI vendor: SOC 2 Type II, the \$10M cyber insurance minimum, data return, certified data destruction, consent to assignment/change of control, and a BAA executed before any PHI flows. Several of the gaps go to HIPAA compliance itself, not just commercial risk.

**Must be resolved before execution (Category A, Priority 1). These are walk-away items:**

- Vaultline would own, and could sell to third parties, "Aggregated De-Identified Data" de-identified to a non-HIPAA standard, through an assignment from Panorama (Issue 2).

- There is no SOC 2 Type II obligation and no audit right, and the only security commitment is "commercially reasonable" safeguards (Issue 3). Breach notice is due 72 hours after Vaultline "confirms" an incident, and Vaultline bears no costs (Issue 4).

- Liability is capped at six months' fees "actually paid." Because fees are paid annually in advance, the cap is about \$0 for roughly half of each contract year, and there are no carve-outs. The consequential-damages waiver is unqualified and expressly covers loss of data (Issue 5).

- The IP indemnity excludes combinations with products Vaultline did not provide. That carve-out captures the MedBridge EHR integration, which is the core use case, and makes the indemnity illusory (Issue 6).

- Cyber insurance is \$5M against the \$10M requirement, and there is no Tech E&O (Issue 7). On exit, Panorama only gets a self-service download, after which Vaultline "may delete" the data, and there is no destruction certification (Issue 8).

- Vaultline may assign the agreement without consent in a merger or acquisition (Issue 9). There is no source code escrow even though Vaultline's reported ARR is about \$72M, below the \$100M threshold (Issue 10). Vaultline alone may terminate for convenience on 180 days' notice (Issue 11).

High-priority Required deviations (Category A, Priority 2): the SLA (99.5% "commercially reasonable efforts," 8 hours/week of excluded maintenance, a 10% credit cap, credits on claim only, sole remedy); 5-business-day deemed acceptance; Net 15 terms with \$1,425,000 prepaid before go-live; escalation at the greater of 5% or CPI-U from Year 2; a 60-day cure period with no PHI-breach termination right; force majeure that covers hosting failures and runs 180 days; Texas law and venue; a 120-day non-renewal notice; a 3-year post-term confidentiality tail; and a narrow Customer Data definition.
